choices.C: Snakes that can add are purple.

question:
Tom has a collection of \(13\) snakes, \(4\) of which are purple and \(5\) of which are happy. He observes that

• all of his happy snakes can add,

• none of his purple snakes can subtract, and

• all of his snakes that can’t subtract also can’t add.

Which of these conclusions can be drawn about Tom’s snakes?
solution:
The third statement forces every snake that can add to be able to subtract. Indeed, if such a snake could not subtract, that statement would say it could not add, a contradiction.

Every happy snake can add, so every happy snake can also subtract. But purple snakes cannot subtract. Consequently, every happy snake must be nonpurple:
\[
\text{happy}\implies\text{can add}\implies\text{can subtract}\implies\text{not purple}.
\]
Thus the conclusion is \(\boxed{\text{Happy snakes are not purple}}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
